2) Scheduling guarantee — Nimbus: 120h stated but no scheduling/availability guarantee in excerpts (question to confirm); Us: we commit resource scheduling in the SOW.  
3) Post‑90 T&M — Nimbus: change‑requests billed T&M with no published hourly rates or caps in the draft (unknown); Us: published T&M rates and pre‑agreed caps/estimates.  
4) SLA / credit usability — Nimbus: credits only if monthly uptime <99.5%, claim within 10 business days, credits capped at 10% of monthly fees (practical recourse is limited by short claim window and cap); Us: SLA credits, clearer remediation steps and longer claim windows to make credits practicable.  
5) Renewal mechanics — Nimbus: contractual cap “up to 7%/yr” but vendor practice (“typically hold flat if usage grows”) is non‑contractual; Us: explicit renewal guardrails tied to usage/metrics.  
6) Termination / refunds — Nimbus: 90‑day notice allowed but prepaid fees are non‑refundable per draft (cash loss risk on early exit); Us: pro‑rata refund/credit treatment for unused prepayments in standard terms.  
7) Day‑1 vs 2‑yr NPV — Nimbus: steep Q4 discount + prepay reduces Day‑1 cost but increases two‑year NPV, overage and exit risk; Us: smaller/milestone discounts and monthly billing lower two‑year cost volatility.  
8) Practical operational risk — Nimbus: SLA claim burdens, credit caps and limited included PS hours increase execution and availability risk; Us: defined TTV commitments, SLAs and PS scope to reduce operational risk.  
9) Recommendation — request contract excerpts on T&M rates, overage caps, scheduling guarantees, SLA evidence requirements, and any renewal exceptions before finalizing economics.  

Unknowns to flag and confirm with Nimbus: exact T&M hourly rates and any overage caps; whether 120 hours is schedulable/guaranteed or subject to resource availability; the precise evidence and process required to trigger SLA credits; any contractual exceptions to the 7% renewal cap; and the mechanics for refunding or crediting unused prepaid fees/PS hours.
